title: listing.v1
description: One VERSION of one ad's page, source-agnostic. Append-only JSONL: a new line is written when an ad_id is first seen, when a list-card fact changes, or when the stored version is older than 7 days. The latest version of an ad is the line with the greatest fetched_at for its (source.site, ad_id). Raw fetches leave text_hint/geocode/city_centre/derived null; `llens derive` fills them in a rebuildable copy. Field names follow schema.org where one exists (GeoCoordinates, datePublished).

ad_id.description: The site's own stable id (from the ad URL). Survives bumps and edits.

fetched_at.description: When this version of the ad page was fetched (UTC).

fetch_reason.description: Why this version exists. `reparse` = re-extracted OFFLINE from the saved snapshot (raw_ref) with a newer parser; fetched_at then stays the page's original fetch time. `panel` = a scheduled revisit of a panel advertiser's ad (the standing approval's panel). `recruit` = a one-off sample of ads seen on list cards but never opened (fetch-ads --select recruit).

raw_ref.description: The gzipped snapshot of the ad page this version was parsed from, under $LLENS_DATA (never in the repo).

region.description: The site's region the ad is listed under (the source's region slug).

description.description: Whole body text, never truncated. Line breaks are kept as \n (the source's parser @3); spaces collapse within a line and blank lines are dropped.

phone_masked.description: Exactly as the page shows it BEFORE 'show' (e.g. the last digits only). The full value is never requested.

email_masked.description: Exactly as shown before 'show' (e.g. the domain only). Never the full address.

website.description: As shown before 'show'; null when the page hides the row.

whatsapp.description: A WhatsApp contact row is shown. The page shows only a button, never a value (the source's parser @4).

media_urls.description: Public URLs only; media is never downloaded.

first_published.description: schema.org datePublished as the page states it (keeps its own offset).

bumped_at.description: Last bump/repost at fetch time, site-local wall time converted with an explicit zone; null if the absolute and relative texts disagree.

city_label.description: The city/area the advertiser filed the ad under (human-chosen).

pin.description: The site's own map pin (schema.org GeoCoordinates when the page carries them; approximate).

site.description: Site-specific facts, one key per source module. The core never depends on these.

derived.description: Recomputable measurements. Never hand-edited; each carries the method that produced it.

location_valid_pin.description: false when the pin is outside the label's region (location_region_test: its census divisions, else > REGION_KM from the label centre); null without a pin or a test.

location_valid_text.description: false when the text geocode is > REGION_KM from the label centre; null without one.

location_invalid_reason.description: Why a location is not usable for this ad; null when nothing is flagged. Raw points are kept. out_of_region_place: the final place point (place_point) is out of region while the raw pin/text are not flagged.

geocode_decision.description: The resolution rule for a precise text point: auto_close (<= AUTO_ACCEPT_KM from a real in-region pin) is accepted; every other value goes to a human place check.

place_decision.description: The place decision applied to this ad (place_apply): operator accept_google | pick_alternative | other_place, machine text_only_verified | auto_alternative | review, derive's auto_close; null for a bare pin or nothing.

place_decided_by.description: operator (a place-review batch), place-check@N, or derive's method (auto_close); null otherwise.

place_decision_status.description: applied: place_point is set by the decision; any other value: the decision did not produce a point, and why.

place_point.description: The final point for this ad (a Google coordinate except for source pin: derived is rebuilt within the 30-day TTL).

place_cache_ref.description: The geocode-cache entry a Google-sourced place_point came from (candidate = index into its candidates, null = the answer itself); export-db re-reads the coordinate through it.

place_gold_v2.description: true: the operator decision is on an address-gold-v2 ad. Never a gold label source.

location_valid_place.description: false when place_point is > REGION_KM from the label centre (flagged, never removed); null without one.

place_osm.description: The OSM fallback for an other_place text whose Google answer was rejected: google (its status), status, names (OSM ways per road), gap_km (closest approach, <= T_osm), near_label (approaches within LABEL_KM of the label centre).

location_region_test.description: Which region test decided location_valid_*: boundary = inside the union of the label's 2021 census divisions (+ EDGE_M), radius = <= REGION_KM from the label centre (a label with no CD mapping); null without a centre or mapping.

raw.description: The location phrase exactly as written in the ad.

kind.description: street = one road with no cross street (or a city + highway); area = a neighbourhood or "airport area". Neither is a point: derive records their geocode as precise=false.

query.description: The geocodable phrase an alias stands for (e.g. a mall abbreviation's full name); absent when raw is geocoded as written.

extractor.description: Which extractor version produced it (method tag).

precise.description: intersection / street_address / premise / establishment / postal_code, i.e. not a centroid.

location_type.description: Google's geometry.location_type: ROOFTOP | RANGE_INTERPOLATED | GEOMETRIC_CENTER | APPROXIMATE (its own confidence in the point).

candidates.description: Up to 3 results of the same request, the answer first, so a human check can pick another match.
